sections.html:
Superior sellers weigh three choices: an agent's listing, a sale you manage alone, or a cash buyer who accepts every flaw. Three things settle it: what the house needs, how fast you must move, and the net you need at the end.

Up here, a buyer's inspector looks first at the roof, siding and heating system. Finish that work first and a listing may reward you. Cash fits an heir, an owner living elsewhere, or anyone who cannot pay for a new roof, siding or furnace. Total up the net on each route once repairs, taxes and the months of upkeep are subtracted.

  • Listing: a bigger audience, more hoops, and weeks on the buyer's lender and inspector.
  • Sale by owner: you name the price and carry the paperwork, condition report included.
  • Cash buyer: a flat as-is price and a closing date written into the offer.

sections.h2: What Superior's housing market looks like
sections.html: Superior is the Douglas County seat, at the western tip of Lake Superior, and it forms the Twin Ports with Duluth, Minnesota. Most housing is owner-occupied: 60.6 percent of units, with a median owner-occupied value of $180,400. The city had an estimated 26,397 people in 2025, 1.3 percent fewer than at the 2020 base, and nearly 18 percent are 65 or older. Superior counts 11,956 households, with median rent at $900 and median household income at $64,216. Your house will land above or below the citywide median depending on condition and location.

Superior winters are severe. Heat loss, ice and snow load are the first things an inspector checks, so gather furnace service tickets, insulation work and any roof or siding invoices.

The city's property standards require heating equipment that holds 68 degrees in habitable rooms and a water heater that supplies 120-degree water at sinks, tubs and showers. Confirm both work before an appraiser or inspector visits.

sections.h2: Which city code items should I fix before selling?
sections.html:
The building inspection office publishes a list of the most commonly violated regulations. It is written for rental owners, but most items also apply to one- and two-family homes that owners live in. Go through them before listing.

  • Address numbers readable from the street day and night.
  • A tight roof with no missing or badly worn shingles, and siding in sound, weathertight condition.
  • Stairs, porches and decks in sound repair, with graspable handrails on stairs of more than three risers.
  • Smoke alarms in each sleeping room, the access area and on each story and in the basement, plus carbon monoxide alarms where state law requires them.
  • Locks on every window within 8 feet of grade.
  • Downspouts and roof drains that connect to the city sanitary sewer must be disconnected and run outside. Contact the Environmental Services Division at 715-394-5826.

Lead-safe work practices are required when painted surfaces are disturbed. Call Building Inspection at 715-395-7288 to ask which permits are on file. The city also runs an online records search covering permits, building inspections and code compliance cases from June 2021 forward.

Anyone selling a building of up to four units owes the buyer a completed condition report, and Chapter 709 sets the deadline at 10 days after the contract is accepted. Late delivery gives the buyer 2 business days to rescind. For any entry in their field, the owner may substitute written information from an engineer, surveyor, pest control operator, qualified third party or contractor.

The seller pays a transfer fee to the state, 30 cents per $100, set out in section 77.22. No city or county may add its own fee on a transfer the state exempts.

sections.h2: Recording at the Douglas County Register of Deeds
sections.html: The Douglas County Register of Deeds is at 1313 Belknap Street, Room 108, Superior, and can be reached at 715-395-1463. Recording a document costs $30 on the county's fee schedule. After a deed is recorded, check with the Real Property Lister that the tax records picked up the right owner and legal description.

sections.h2: Property taxes and a Superior sale
sections.html:
The city treasurer sends tax bills in mid to late December, and a seller should know the schedule well because it affects the closing split. You may pay the whole bill at once or in two parts.

Payment optionDue dateIf missed
Full payment or first installmentJanuary 31July option is lost; interest of 1 percent per month runs on the whole balance from February 1
Second installmentJuly 31Available only when the first installment was paid on time

The Lottery and Gaming Credit goes only to a primary residence, so rental or other properties do not qualify.

Delinquent taxes matter before a sale. Under state law the county may take a tax deed after two years, though its current practice is a four-year cycle, and that could change. If back taxes are owed, the Douglas County Treasurer can quote a payoff. Get the number before you say yes to any offer, so that the net you compare is real. At closing your title company settles the balance from your proceeds.

A cash buyer may be able to close before a tax deed becomes a danger, and that is a real reason owners behind on taxes look at that route. The written offer should still say who pays the back taxes and the recording costs, and you should ask for the closing date in writing.

sections.h2: Getting a Superior house ready to show
sections.html:
Lake Superior winters leave marks, so give the buyer proof the house was cared for. Pull furnace tickets, insulation receipts and roof or siding invoices into one folder. Test the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, check the window locks, and make sure the address numbers can be read from the street at night.

If downspouts tie into the sewer, disconnect them and run them outside as the city requires, and keep the call to the Environmental Services Division on your list. An inspector who finds nothing to flag makes a buyer's lender more comfortable, and it leaves less room for a price cut late in the deal.

sections.h2: From contract to closing in Superior
sections.html: Accepting an offer starts the report deadline, so finish the form early. Gather furnace and roof records, permit answers from Building Inspection, and a payoff figure for any loan or tax balance. Meanwhile the title company runs the record search, drafts the deed and files the transfer return online. Closing is where you sign, and the deed then goes on record at the register's office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Superior house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take the house as it is, while a listing buyer may ask for repairs. Ask Building Inspection at 715-395-7288 whether any notice is open on the address, and answer the condition report honestly about known defects.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer fee on a Superior home sale?
faqs.a: The rate is 30 cents for every $100 of value, paid by the seller. Douglas County's register takes it at recording once the electronic return is filed.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Douglas County?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars on the county schedule, with the transfer fee on top. A call to 715-395-1463 confirms the total before you mail anything.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Superior?
faqs.a: Full payment or the first installment is due January 31, and the second installment July 31. Miss the January date and interest of 1 percent a month runs from February 1 on the entire balance.

faqs.q: Does the seller owe the buyer a condition report in Superior?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Chapter 709 gives you 10 days from contract acceptance, and a buyer who gets it late can cancel within 2 business days. Representatives and trustees who never lived there are exempt.
